subject: Recap: Renewal & burst-capacity options + next steps
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Riley Park <riley@bluespanhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 May 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Renewal & burst-capacity options + next steps

Hi Riley / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid run-through of where BlueSpan is with inference right now. Quick recap to lock in what we discussed and proposed next steps. Tone: actionable.

Summary of pain points you called out:
- Production latency spikes during nightly claim ingestion windows (15–45m tail).
- Rising per-token costs for nightly RAG pipelines; large embedding footprint for search.
- Compliance requirement: encrypted logs for three months and SOC2 attestation for vendor onboarding.
- Renewal for the hosted account is ~90 days out; you want usage predictability before committing.

Goals you articulated:
- Reduce tail latency in batch windows to keep SLA at 99th < 2s for interactive features.
- Cut per-token spend on nightly jobs by 30–40% via batching/caching or a reserved option.
- Prove deterministic performance in a 6-week pilot with measurable cost delta.

What we proposed (next phases):
1) Short pilot (4–6 weeks): Dedicated reserved pool evaluation for your nightly inference load (pin model variant + quantization profile).
   - We’ll enable prefix/KV caching and an autoscale headroom policy for burst ingestion.
2) Parallel RAG cost test: run the same ingestion on hosted vs dedicated for two weeks to compare unit economics and latencies.
3) Security & procurement: we'll share SOC2 artifacts and an MSA with minimal redlines; you share procurement timeline and any legal must-haves.

Immediate action items (owners & timeline):
- (Action: Laura) Send you the usage CSV and initial dedicated pricing worksheet — attached. (Today)
- (Action: Ben) Draft pilot SOW + target SLOs and preliminary cost comparison. (By 5/22)
- (Action: Mina) Pull SOC2 docs, security questionnaire answers, and an artifact bundle. (By 5/21)
- (Action: Riley/Samir) Confirm procurement lead/POC and whether a PO will be required before pilot. (By 5/23)

Attachments included: usage_report_apr_may_2025.csv (raw token + request traces), redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.xlsx (starter worksheet), proposed_msa_redlines.pdf (for legal).

Proposed next meeting: 30-min alignment call week of 5/26 to finalize SOW and pilot start date. I can send a Doodle if that works.

If I mis-stated anything, flag it and I’ll correct. Otherwise I’ll push the attachments and Ben/Mina will follow with their pieces.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0143

Redwood Inference — helping engineering teams run reliable, cost-predictable LLM inference

From: Riley Park <riley@bluespanhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir@bluespanhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Renewal & burst-capacity options + next steps

Hi Laura — thanks for the recap and for moving quickly. Couple quick clarifications: 

- Procurement: I’m looping in our procurement lead (not on this thread yet) but the timeline is roughly 2–3 weeks to approve a pilot SOW; a PO is optional for the pilot but likely required for any multi-month commit.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II is sufficient, and we’ll need a short security addendum for log retention and KMS integration.

We’re fine to run the parallel cost test and pilot as you outlined. Please make the pilot SOW explicit about what success metrics look like (latency percentiles, cost per 1M tokens for batch run).

I’ll confirm internal POC by Friday. Schedule the 5/26 alignment call — midday PST works best.

Thanks,
Riley Park
Director of ML Ops | BlueSpan Health
riley@bluespanhealth.com

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap: Renewal & burst-capacity options + next steps

Ben / Mina — forwarding Riley’s note + thread. Attached the usage CSV and my starter pricing worksheet in case you want to iterate offline. 

Ben: please draft a 1-page pilot SOW that includes:
- Pilot scope: nightly ingestion workload (hours window + average seq len)
- Success metrics: 99th latency target, cost delta target (target 30% reduction), and sample queries for verification
- Pilot duration & start window: propose 6 weeks, start as early as 6/2 if procurement clears

Mina: can you pull the SOC2 bundle and KMS integration notes into a single zip for them? Also flag any security-blocking items for dedicated/private deployment.

I’ll schedule the 5/26 call and invite Riley/Samir + their procurement contact when provided.

-L

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Riley Park <riley@bluespanhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Renewal & burst-capacity options + next steps

Thanks Laura — on it. Draft SOW (1-pager) will be in your inbox by EOD 5/22. Initial numbers: assuming a dedicated r5-like pool with KV caching we estimate ~35% cost reduction for nightly batch at current volumes — will validate once we run the comparative two-week test.

Also attaching a short note on pilot telemetry we’ll collect (tail latency histograms, token accounting by stage, cold-start traces).

Riley: if you can share the procurement POC, I’ll include any billing/legal checkpoints in the SOW.
